standard_prerequisites.name: Tutte-Berge formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: The matching deficiency equals max over U of odd(G minus U) minus |U|.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Source237-243, citing Berge1962; the exact formula is printed as allowed context.
standard_prerequisites.use: Translate bounds on odd components, and the explicit constructed obstruction, into matching existence/nonexistence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical Cartesian-product edge-connectivity formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: For connected regular factors of sizes M_i and total degree d, lambda(product)=min(d,min_i lambda(H_i) product_(j!=i) M_j).
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Source318-335, citing Hammack, Imrich and Klavzar, Handbook of Product Graphs (2011), Chapter5.
standard_prerequisites.use: This exact classical structural formula is explicitly permitted; its proof is not part of the counted task.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary finite counting and real inequalities
standard_prerequisites.use: Parity of a cut, exponential-versus-linear estimates, and the number/order of Cartesian-product components.

core_obligations: Convert edge-connectivity >=d-1 into Tutte-Berge control using parity of every odd-component boundary, then show the product reaches this threshold.
Build the regular m-branch obstruction H and amplify by triangles while preserving odd components so 3^(t-1)<m violates Tutte.

proof_roadmap.step: Odd component boundary has parity d, so a d-1 cut lower bound gives d; sum its edges into U and apply Tutte-Berge.
Lift a factor matching if possible; otherwise all factors have order at least3, and product edge-connectivity grows exponentially with dimension.
Build the m-regular hub graph on (m+1)^2 vertices from m copies of the odd-order gadget. Its product with t-1 triangles has m odd components after removing only 3^(t-1) hub vertices.

difficulty_reason: The parity upgrade plus explicit regular obstruction survive the allowed classical connectivity formula and Tutte-Berge inputs. The upper/lower threshold proof forms one H2 task. Source maximal/maximum wording is disclosed; asymptotic lower bound is not silently strengthened to all small M.

compared.difference: The existing counted claim controls a Gallai-Edmonds obstruction in random nonbipartite product graphs. This task is the deterministic threshold and explicit lower construction, with no random graph, sprinkling or decomposition estimates.

editorial_notes: The Cartesian edge-connectivity formula and Tutte-Berge formula are explicit permitted classical inputs. The quantitative threshold and the regular obstruction construction remain proof obligations.
The statement uses t>2 ln M, as printed in source103, rather than the weak inequality used in the abstract.

The phrase maximal matching in the last sentence of the auxiliary proof365 refers to a maximum matching: the displayed Tutte-Berge deficiency is defined for a maximum matching in source239. The author text is retained.
The lower-bound construction is phrased for sufficiently large M in source381. It establishes constant-factor asymptotic sharpness; the editorial title does not add a claim at small M.
The source disclosure at1686-1687 is retained: AI tools were used for polishing, while the authors state that all proof ideas were entirely human-generated.

editorial_scope: One deterministic two-sided dimension theorem, with its complete regular-graph lemma, lower-bound construction and native diagram. Random-process hitting times and their proof lemmas are outside this task.

source_authorship.known_AI_disclosure: Explicit source1686-1687: AI polishing, all proof ideas entirely human-generated; disclosure included visibly.

review_checkpoints: After assuming no factor has a perfect matching, each nontrivial connected factor has at least3 vertices; the M=2 case was already removed. For M=3,4 the first relevant t=3 can be checked directly; the exponential bound then increases relative to t(M-1).
In the lower gadget m is odd, H-prime has m+2 odd vertices, its unique degree-(m-1) vertex is x, and adding the hub edge repairs exactly that deficit.
Deleting the hub layer in H square K3^(t-1) gives exactly m odd components, each of order (m+2)3^(t-1). The whole graph has even order.
The proof calls the lower construction asymptotic; do not silently strengthen its small-parameter quantifiers.
